summary: Most of your blood counts are in the healthy range. Your hemoglobin is a little low, which can make you feel tired and is often linked to low iron. It's worth discussing with your doctor.

tests.name: Hemoglobin
tests.explanation: Hemoglobin carries oxygen in your blood; yours is below the usual range.

tests.name: RBC count
tests.explanation: The number of red blood cells is in the healthy range.

tests.name: Hematocrit
tests.explanation: The share of your blood made up of red cells is normal.

tests.name: WBC count
tests.explanation: White blood cells fight infection; your count is normal.

tests.name: Neutrophils
tests.explanation: The most common infection-fighting cells are in the normal range.

tests.name: Platelet count
tests.explanation: Platelets help your blood clot; your count is healthy.

tests.name: Platelet morphology
tests.explanation: Your platelets look normal under the microscope.

keyFindings: Hemoglobin is low at 10.8 g/dL (usual range 13 - 17), which suggests mild anemia.
White blood cells and platelets are normal.
questionsForDoctor: Could my low hemoglobin be caused by low iron or vitamin B12?
Do I need further tests such as serum ferritin?
When should I repeat this blood test?
generalTips: Include iron-rich foods like leafy greens, lentils and jaggery in your meals.
Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C sources such as citrus fruits to help absorption.
